limitations: results on emotional response remain fragmented and inconsistent.
PCM cannot sufficiently distinguish between some of the mood/emotional categories.
facial expressions... insufficient at distinguishing emotions beyond the obvious types.
physiological response... hard to correlate these changes to specific emotions.
forcing participants to evaluate sound clips or sound environments through audio replay... ignores peoples' implicit emotional reactions.
behaviour observation method... could introduce the Hawthorne effect.
sampling biases... affect the generalisation of the study results.
POMS was originally developed in a medical context.
absence of an actual performer, leading to a reduction in eventfulness in a laboratory context.
sound clips were designed with a combination of sound types. Therefore, the design limited the investigation of individual sound types.
many different sound sources within each sound type category. This study only recorded a single source for each studied sound type.
sound appropriateness... beyond the scope of this study.
more dimensions in the soundscape study of mood states exists than simply pleasantness and eventfulness.
Whether the conclusions of this research can be extended to other music types will require further study.
